summary: C. W. Huntington, Jr. worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).
Caixi Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, studying at Presidency University (~1928–1934) under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held posts at the Government Museum, Chennai (1935–1946), Indian Museum (1946), Archaeological Survey of India (~1946–1955), and National Museum, New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Friends Seminary, Harvard (undergraduate ~1950–1954; PhD ~1954–1959), EPHE, and DIAS. He held professorships at Harvard (1959–2003) and UCLA (2003–2013), and founded the East Coast Indo-European Conference in 1982.

Cameron Bailey specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, Jimmy Yu, Kathleen M. Erndl, Joseph Hellweg, and Richard F. Nance, and at the University of Oxford under Ulrike Roesler.

Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Yudru Tsomu. He has held academic posts at Middlebury College, Dickinson College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018) under Bryan J. Cuevas and Jimmy Yu, later becoming a postdoctoral fellow at Columbia University (attested 2026).

Camillo Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan. He has held positions at the University of Cambridge (2011–2014), SOAS University of London, the Bodleian Library (attested 2019), and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Carel Gabriel Cobet was a Dutch scholar of linguistics. Educated at Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University (~1832–1840), he held posts at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884, teaching Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Willem Caland.

Carl A. P. Ruck works in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1956–1959) and Harvard University (~1961–1965), and held a post at Boston University (~1970).

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki (~1966–1971), Seizan Yanagida, and earned a PhD at UC Berkeley. He served on the faculty at Stanford University (~1980–2013; emeritus ~2013).

Carl Cappeller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber at Berlin (1860–1864), Königsberg (~1864–1868), Leipzig (PhD ~1868), and Jena (habilitation ~1871–1872). He became a professor at Jena in 1875.
Carl Christian Rafn was a Danish scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1814–1816) and later held a post there (~1820–1826).

Carl Darling Buck was a linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (1892–1933), where he taught Leonard Bloomfield and Fang-Kuei Li.

Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at TU Braunschweig, Göttingen (under Lichtenberg and Heyne, 1795–1798), and Helmstedt (PhD 1798–1807). From 1807 to 1855, he served as full professor at the University of Göttingen and director of the Göttingen Observatory.
Carl Gaedicke is an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877, studying under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Gustav Jung was a Swiss scholar of religious studies and philosophy. After medical studies at the University of Basel (1895–1900), he held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1913), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

Carl Olson is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig (PhD ~1834–1842) under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Berlin (~1838–1841). He served at the University of Oslo as Lektor (1847) and professor (1857).
Carl Schuster was an American scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Harvard University (~1923–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1930–1934).
